correctness.rationale: For every quantified p,q,k,a and 0<E<Ec, strict radial monotonicity gives one smooth inner oval. Integer-frequency changes preserve angular Lebesgue integrals exactly, so area and Hamiltonian coarea period coincide. Every nonzero equilibrium is exactly a negative angular extremum at radius rc and is a nondegenerate saddle. Uniform local Morse expansion proves an individual saddle time coefficient (1/k)sqrt(q/d)rc^(2-p), while the complement has uniformly bounded time. Summation and exact k-fold rotational symmetry prove the logarithmic law and atomic weak measure limit. The standalone checker confirms specific algebraic identities, but the proof is analytic.

value.rationale: A natural full family of polynomial Hamiltonians shares its complete physical period-energy and area functions while admitting arbitrarily different separatrix saddle multiplicities (within the degree allowance) and mutually distinct time-measure endpoint limits. This isolates information that a global period function cannot recover; the five-degree 1/3/5 saddle triple is an explicit low-degree witness, and the cancellation law is exact, not a routine parameter increment.
